title: The Pressure Recipe
brief: Meridian Microworks engineering proposes raising polish pressure in recipe PR-12 by 10 percent to shorten cycle time. Change ECN-55 is due for approval. You have 12 visit points to assess the change for risks, controls, and records.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Shift lead: how the change will be introduced
Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: ECN-55 states the reason, recipe, products, and approvers.
Experiment results: 12 wafers; flatness measured on 12, but edge defects and particle counts not measured. No acceptance criteria.
evidence.whyItMatters: The change must be shown not to affect all relevant characteristics.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check every characteristic the change could affect.

evidence.text: Customer terms PCN-1 require 90 days' notice of process changes for qualified products; ECN-55 gives none.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer change notification requirements must be met.

evidence.text: Customer specification lists flatness, edge, and particle limits.
Process risk analysis for polish (PRA-3) does not include pressure as a factor and was last updated 2 years ago.
evidence.whyItMatters: Risks from the change must be identified and addressed.
evidence.missedExplanation: Link the change to the risk analysis.

evidence.text: Recipe system access: 14 users can edit recipes, including 6 operators; recipe change approval is not enforced.
evidence.whyItMatters: Recipe changes need control so only approved versions are used.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask who can change a recipe.

evidence.text: Recipe history shows PR-12 version 9 was edited twice last month with the comment "test".
evidence.whyItMatters: Unexplained edits suggest weak control; investigate.

evidence.text: Flatness measurement capability study was done at the old pressure; gauge repeatability uses 30 percent of tolerance.
evidence.whyItMatters: Measurement must be capable for the changed process.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask whether the measurement can see the effect.

evidence.text: Shift lead: "We'd just load the new recipe." No training or communication plan is attached to ECN-55.
evidence.whyItMatters: A communication plan supports consistent introduction.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask how people will learn of the change.

evidence.text: Recipe names use an old abbreviation style.
evidence.whyItMatters: Naming style is not a requirement.

evidence.text: Flatness gauge FG-2 is calibrated, due in 5 months.
evidence.whyItMatters: The gauge is calibrated; capability is the separate question.

evidence.text: Equipment paint is worn on the cover.

options: No. Return it with conditions: full characteristic testing with criteria, updated risk analysis, measurement capability, recipe access control, training, and customer notice
Approve for one tool only without notice
decisions.rationale: The benefit can be kept once the review is complete.

containment: Keep PR-12 at the approved version and restrict recipe edit access
correction: Complete the testing, risk update, capability study, training, and customer notice
cause: Recipe changes are not enforced through approval, and the change form lacks risk and customer prompts
corrective: Enforce recipe approval in the system and add risk, measurement, and customer notice prompts to ECN forms
effectiveness: Audit recipe edits and ECN completeness monthly for three months

debriefText.found: You assessed the change against characteristics, risk, measurement, access, and customer terms.
debriefText.missed: Ask who can change a recipe as well as whether this change is sound.
debriefText.falseFinding: Naming style and paint are not findings.
